fact: Webb Fontaine says it completed migration of Benin's national Customs Management System from ASYCUDA to Webb Customs, fully operational at all sea ports, airports and land border offices, with over 100,000 declarations processed.

Webb Fontaine says it launched Benin's Guichet Unique du Commerce Extérieur (Single Window) in 2018, and that the government is interconnecting the Single Window, Port Community System, Electronic Cargo Tracking and the Customs Management System.

Benin Customs says the GUCE single window, operational since 2018, handles import declarations with online issue of agencies' authorisations, licences and certificates, and was officially handed to government on 21 July 2023.
Benin Customs says the GUCE lets it process customs declarations and electronic payment of import and export declarations.
Benin Customs says clearance at the port of Cotonou and at land borders now runs through GUCE, with Hilacondji clearance dematerialised and cut from 18 steps to 10.
Benin Customs says GUCE is the single platform for international trade operations, connecting all administrations and technical directorates, with more than 2,000 users.
Webb Fontaine says Webb Customs has replaced Sydonia World in Benin, with fully automated customs procedures, and at the Hilla-Condji border all formalities are completed online.

Webb Fontaine says a reform in January 2018 created the Foreign Trade Single Window (GUCE), merging the Port Single Window, the Foreign Trade Operations Single Window and Sydonia World into one interface.

Webb Fontaine says Webb Customs, launched in July 2022, has replaced ASYCUDA World at 44 of Benin's 49 customs offices, with the last five including the port of Cotonou planned for mid-2025; it reports 59,000 returns processed and 100,000 receipts issued.
Webb Fontaine says Webb Customs interconnects trade platforms including the National Single Window, the Port Community System and electronic cargo tracking.

ECOWAS said its Interconnected System for the Management of Goods in Transit (SIGMAT) is installed in the customs IT systems of every ECOWAS member state except Guinea-Bissau and Cabo Verde, and launched its deployment between Benin and Nigeria at Seme-Kraké.
ECOWAS says Benin was connected to the SIGMAT goods-in-transit data exchange system for its customs administration in July 2024.

Webb Fontaine's Benin representative said at the 29 January 2025 public-finance review that Customs Webb, replacing Sydonia World, is used in 44 of 49 customs offices, with 59,000 declarations processed and over 30 billion FCFA collected.
